title: Locally finite type residual substack at a finite-type point
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme, $\mathcal X$ an algebraic stack over $S$, and $x\in|\mathcal X|$ a finite-type point, meaning that some field-valued representative $\operatorname{Spec}L\to\mathcal X$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-field, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. There exist a reduced locally Noetherian algebraic stack $\mathcal Z$ over $S$ and a representable-by-algebraic-spaces monomorphism $i:\mathcal Z\to\mathcal X$ which is locally of finite type, such that $|\mathcal Z|$ has exactly one point and its image is $x$. Here a monomorphism means that $i:\mathcal Z(T)\to\mathcal X(T)$ is fully faithful for every $S$-scheme $T$. No Noetherian hypothesis on $S$ or $\mathcal X$ is required. An algebraic stack over $S$ means a stack in groupoids with diagonal representable by algebraic spaces and a smooth surjective scheme atlas; stack, 2-fibre product, and representability use [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids, def-trf-algebraic-space], and smooth uses [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Its point set consists of field-valued objects modulo isomorphism over a common field extension. A stack is reduced and locally Noetherian when it admits a smooth surjective scheme atlas which is reduced and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]; reduced means every local ring has no nonzero nilpotents. Properties of representable morphisms are tested after scheme base change on etale scheme charts.

source.place: Tag 06G3 (lemma-point-finite-type-monomorphism), (1) implies (3); stacks-properties.tex Tag 06MT (lemma-residual-gerbe), final assertion, and Tag 06MU (definition-residual-gerbe), following paragraph.

proof.text: Choose the locally finite type representative $a:u=\operatorname{Spec}L\to\mathcal X$ from the hypothesis. By definition $\mathcal X$ is an etale stack with diagonal representable by algebraic spaces and a smooth surjective scheme atlas; the etale-to-fppf descent lemma makes it an fppf stack, so $\mathcal X$ is an algebraic stack in the fppf sense required by the self-relation, quotient and source-descent lemmas used below. The diagonal/space-source lemma makes $a$ representable by algebraic spaces. The self-relation quotient lemma gives an algebraic space $R=u\times_{\mathcal X}u$ and its groupoid structure. Both projections $R\to u$ are base changes of $a$, hence locally of finite type by representable base-change calculus. No closed-point or Noetherian-base hypothesis is needed.

source.place: Tag 06G3, first construction paragraph, using the locally finite type field representative already in the hypothesis. The fppf stack condition on $\mathcal X$ is criteria.tex Tag 076V (lemma-stacks-etale).

proof.text: Both projections $R\to u$ are flat and locally finitely presented. Indeed choose an etale scheme atlas of $R$, then affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}B$ in it. The chart criterion makes each $B$ a finite-type $L$-algebra. A field is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0$ and $L$), so the cited finite-type-algebra lemma makes $B$ finitely presented over $L$. Flatness follows directly from the existence of bases of vector spaces over $L$: tensoring an injection with a free vector space is a direct sum of injections. The chart criterion for flatness and local finite presentation now gives both properties for each projection. These are the chart arguments of Tag 06G4, with no assumption on $S$.

source.place: Tag 06G3, flat and locally finitely presented self-relation paragraph; spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 06G4 (lemma-noetherian-finite-type-finite-presentation).

proof.text: Form $\mathcal Z=[u/R]$. Apply the flat-groupoid quotient theorem to step 2: $\mathcal Z$ is algebraic and $q:u\to\mathcal Z$ is representable, surjective, flat and locally finitely presented. Being an fppf stackification, $\mathcal Z$ is an fppf stack, hence also an etale stack because etale coverings are fppf coverings; so it is algebraic in the sense of the statement and in the fppf sense of the self-relation lemma. The self-relation quotient lemma supplies $i:\mathcal Z\to\mathcal X$, $i q\simeq a$, fully faithful on every fibre groupoid; since the quotient is algebraic, $i$ is representable by algebraic spaces. Thus $i$ is the required monomorphism.

source.place: Tag 06G3, quotient construction, using criteria.tex Tags 06FI and 06FH and algebraic.tex Tag 04T4.

proof.text: The spectrum $u$ is reduced, since a field has no nonzero nilpotents, and locally Noetherian, since its only ideals are $0,L$. Apply reduced/locally-Noetherian descent to the fppf scheme cover $q$ to obtain a reduced locally Noetherian smooth scheme atlas of $\mathcal Z$. Its assumptions concern the cover and not the base $S$.

The point set of $u$ has one element: the zero ideal is its only prime ideal. Surjectivity of $q$ means that every field object of $\mathcal Z$ lifts after a field extension to $u$; hence every point of $\mathcal Z$ is the image of that one point. The object $q$ over $u$ supplies a point, so the point set is a nonempty singleton. From $i q\simeq a$ its image in $|\mathcal X|$ is exactly $x$.

source.place: Tag 06G3, quotient construction and its singleton image, unpacked with field-point equivalence.

proof.text: Apply representable local-finite-type source descent with $h=q$, $g=i$. The two morphisms are representable by step 3, $q$ is surjective flat locally finitely presented, and $i q\simeq a$ is locally of finite type by choice. Therefore $i$ is locally of finite type. Together with steps 3--5 this proves all the assertions, without any Noetherian hypothesis on $S$ or $\mathcal X$.

source.place: Tag 06G3, final fppf descent paragraph; use spaces-descent.tex Tag 06EW, not its printed reference to Tag 06EV.

lean.statement: theorem exists_finiteTypePoint_residualSubstack {S : Scheme.{u}} (F : BasedCategory.{v, w} (Over S)) (hF : IsAlgebraicModuliStack F) (x : ModuliPoints F) (hfinite : ∃ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (b : Spec (.of L) ⟶ S) (a : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj (Over.mk b))) F), ModuliSpaceTest (@LocallyOfFiniteType) a ∧ x ∈ Set.range (moduliPointMap a)) : ∃ (Z : BasedCategory.{v, w} (Over S)) (i : BasedFunctor Z F), IsAlgebraicModuliStack Z ∧ IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces i ∧ (∀ T : Over S, (moduliFiberMap i T).Full ∧ (moduliFiberMap i T).Faithful) ∧ ModuliSpaceTest (@LocallyOfFiniteType) i ∧ (∃ (U : Over S) (q : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj U)) Z), IsSmoothModuliAtlas Z U q ∧ IsReduced U.left ∧ IsLocallyNoetherian U.left) ∧ Nonempty (Unique (ModuliPoints Z)) ∧ Set.range (moduliPointMap i) = {x}
